queue.li_title: DSCR Cash-Out Refinance Seasoning: 3, 6, and 12 Months
queue.li_desc: Why seasoning windows exist, what they cost investors, and what each window really costs a BRRRR investor.
queue.li:
The number that decides how fast a BRRRR investor scales isn't the rehab budget or the ARV. It's the seasoning window.

Most DSCR lenders require 6-12 months of ownership before a cash-out refinance can use the new appraised value. That's 6-12 months of your capital parked in a finished, rented property doing nothing.

Our window is 3 months. No lease required at closing — the market-rent appraisal qualifies.

On a $110K cash-in deal, getting your capital back at month 3 instead of month 6 is the difference between four cycles a year and two. At portfolio scale, that compounds into an entirely different growth curve.

queue.li_title: DSCR Loans for Airbnb & Short-Term Rentals: How Financing Actually Works
queue.li_desc: How lenders qualify STR income, why market rent is the conservative anchor, and the STR-specific traps to avoid.
queue.li:
Short-term rentals can out-earn long-term rents two-to-one in the right market. Try explaining that to a bank.

Conventional lenders qualify you, not the property. They ignore projected nightly revenue and cap how many financed doors you can hold. So STR investors end up on DSCR loans, where the property qualifies itself.

The real question in short-term rental underwriting is which income number goes in the numerator. Some lenders will underwrite documented nightly-rate history, then charge for it with rate premiums, larger reserve requirements, and a haircut of 20% or more on the revenue — because nightly income is seasonal, volatile, and one city-council vote away from a licensing problem.

We use the conservative anchor instead: the appraiser's long-term market rent. If the property covers its payment as a plain 12-month rental, it qualifies. No lease required, no host history required, and every dollar you earn above market rent stays yours rather than becoming leverage priced against you.

A property that only works at 78% occupancy and peak nightly rates doesn't fail our underwriting. It fails risk management, and we would rather say so before you own it.

DSCR rates start at 6.80% on a 30-year fixed, and you close in your LLC.

queue.li_title: Fix & Flip Loans for Beginners: Financing Your First Deal
queue.li_desc: What lenders expect from a first-timer, realistic leverage, the draw process, and the four mistakes that sink first flips.
queue.li:
Nobody funds your fiftieth flip because of your fiftieth flip. They fund it because somebody funded your first one.

First-time flippers do get financed by private lenders. What changes with experience is not access — it is leverage. Experienced borrowers reach up to 92.5% loan-to-cost with us. A first-timer should plan on starting around 85%, which means bringing roughly 15% of total project cost plus reserves. That is not the lender hazing you. Skin in the game on deal one is what keeps a rough first project from becoming a foreclosure instead of a lesson.

What gets underwritten on a first deal:

The numbers — purchase price plus rehab budget against a defensible after-repair value, with total cost landing under roughly 70 to 75% of ARV so there is margin for holding costs and surprises.

Your liquidity — down payment, closing costs, carrying costs for the full timeline, and a contingency of 10 to 15% of the rehab budget. On a $250K project, plan on $50K to $60K accessible.

Your credit — best pricing at 720 and up, solid at 680.

Your team — a licensed GC bid instead of a guess. First-timers who show up with a real scope of work get treated like second-timers.

The rehab money is not handed over at closing. It sits in escrow and releases in draws as work is completed and inspected, which protects you as much as it protects us. Nobody can spend the framing budget before framing exists.

Bridge terms run 6 to 18 months, interest-only, from 9.5%, with closings in as little as 72 hours and a $100K minimum loan size.

queue.li_title: Buying Rental Property in an LLC: How Investor Loans Actually Close
queue.li_desc: Why investors close in an entity, the personal guaranty, the five documents that make an LLC close fast, and the conventional-loan trap.
queue.li:
Every asset-protection attorney says the same thing: hold your rentals in an LLC. Then the investor calls their bank and hears “we can't lend to an LLC.” Both are right, and the gap between them is exactly where investor lending lives.

Conventional Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac mortgages are consumer products. The rules generally require title in your personal name, qualify you on personal debt-to-income, and cap you at ten financed properties. Deeding a conventionally financed house into your LLC after closing works right up until a lender decides to invoke the due-on-sale clause.

DSCR loans are business-purpose loans, so lending to entities is the default rather than the exception. The LLC is the borrower and holds title from day one. The members sign a personal guaranty and credit is pulled on the guarantors — the entity shields you from tenant lawsuits and property liabilities, not from your own loan. Pricing is identical to lending to an individual, because the loan qualifies on the property's rent and the guarantors' credit either way.

What the structure buys you: liability separation, no ten-property cap, portfolio loans that blanket 2 to 10 properties on one note, and an operating agreement that handles partner splits so the loan does not have to.

Five documents make an entity close fast, and having them ready as PDFs before you go under contract is most of the trick: articles of organization, a signed and current operating agreement, the EIN letter, a recent certificate of good standing, and identification for every guarantor.

DSCR rates start at 6.80% on a 30-year fixed, with a $100K minimum loan size.

queue.li_title: Spec Home Construction Loans for Investors: How Ground-Up Financing Works
queue.li_desc: Land plus vertical financing, the two leverage tests, draw schedules, interest on drawn balance, and planning the exit before you break ground.
queue.li:
On an 18-month ground-up build, the term that moves the most money isn't the rate. It's whether interest accrues on the full loan commitment from day one or only on the balance you have actually drawn.

Run the difference. A $600K construction budget where you have drawn $120K for the foundation costs you interest on $120K under drawn-balance terms and interest on $600K under the other kind. Over a year and a half, that gap is a line item large enough to decide whether the spec pencils. Drawn-balance interest is standard on well-structured private construction loans. Read the term sheet for exactly that line before you sign.

The rest of how spec financing is built:

Two leverage tests set your loan. A loan-to-cost ceiling of 85% on land plus vertical, and a completed-value ceiling that typically runs 65 to 70% of the finished appraised value. Your loan is the lesser of the two. A cheap lot with an efficient build clears both comfortably. A premium lot with a luxury build hits the completed-value cap first, which means more cash in. Run both tests before you buy the dirt.

Draws follow milestones. Land funds at closing. The construction budget sits in escrow and releases against foundation, framing and dry-in, mechanicals, drywall and finishes, and final. Photos and invoices in, an app-based inspection confirms percent complete, funds wire in days. Most ground-up builds run 4 to 7 draws.

Plan both exits before you break ground. Sell into a completed-value appraisal that leaves margin after construction interest, points, and commissions, or hold and refinance the finished home into a 30-year DSCR loan and keep it as a brand-new rental. A spec that pencils both ways has no bad outcome.

Our construction box: land plus vertical up to 85% of project cost, from 10%, 18 or 24 month terms, loans from $100K to $7.5M, 42 states. Own the lot free and clear and its equity usually counts toward your contribution.

queue.li_title: DSCR Loan vs. Conventional Mortgage for Rental Property: Which Should Investors Use?
queue.li_desc: Rates, qualification, the 10-property cap, LLC vesting, and speed — compared honestly, including when conventional still wins.
queue.li:
Your first rental got a conventional mortgage. You had a W-2, the bank said yes, the rate was good. Somewhere around rental three or four, that same bank starts saying no.

The difference in one sentence: a conventional investment mortgage qualifies you — your tax returns, your debt-to-income ratio. A DSCR loan qualifies the property — does its rent cover its payment? Everything else follows from that.

Head to head:

Qualification. Conventional wants two years of returns and DTI under roughly 45% counting every property you own. DSCR wants rent divided by PITIA at 1.0 or better, plus your credit score. No income documents.

Rate. Conventional usually wins, though investment-property pricing adjustments narrow the gap. Our DSCR 30-year fixed starts at 6.80% for the highest credit tier with DSCR 1.20+, before buy down.

Property cap. Fannie Mae stops at ten financed properties and most banks tap out well before that. DSCR has no cap. This is the wall growing investors actually hit.

Title. Conventional generally wants your personal name on it. DSCR closes in your LLC as standard.

Cash-out seasoning. Conventional says 12 months. We say 3.

Here is the part most lenders skip: conventional is still the right call when you have a strong W-2, you are under the property cap, you are fine holding title personally, and you might sell within a couple of years. First or second rental with clean finances? Take the rate edge.

And a reality check on that edge. Half a point lower on a $250K loan is roughly $80 a month. Against that: no tax-return scramble, title in your entity, no property cap, a 3-month refinance instead of 12, and closing weeks faster on a competitive deal. For someone building a portfolio, $80 a month is the cheapest problem on the list.

Most investors don't choose DSCR because it's cheaper. They choose it because it's the loan that lets them keep buying.

queue.li_title: DSCR Calculator: The Formula, a Live Calculator, and What Lenders Count | SLA Capital
queue.li_desc: Run your deal through the live calculator, learn the exact formula, and the five levers when the ratio comes up short.
queue.li:
DSCR is the one ratio that decides whether a rental loan qualifies, and most investors compute it wrong the first time.

The formula is monthly rent divided by PITIA, which is principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and association dues. That is the entire test. No vacancy factor, no maintenance reserve, no property management fee. Lenders run gross rent against the full payment. Your own investment analysis should absolutely subtract those costs. The lender's ratio does not.

The rent number is where the second surprise lives. A lender uses the lower of the lease in place or the appraiser's market-rent report on Form 1007. A vacant property qualifies on the 1007 alone at SLA, with no lease required before you refinance. A short-term rental is anchored to long-term market rent, which means the Airbnb upside stays yours instead of being underwritten and then haircut.

When the ratio comes up short, five levers are worth working before you walk away from the deal. Put more down and cut principal and interest directly. Move to a five-year interest-only structure, which often moves a 0.98 to 1.10 or better. Buy the rate down with points if the hold is long. Challenge the 1007 with documented comparable leases if the appraiser missed recent rentals. Shop taxes and insurance, because fifty dollars a month of premium is worth two to three points of DSCR on a typical deal.

A 1.0 qualifies. Below 1.0 is not an automatic decline here, because we run a below-1.0 lane with additional reserves or a rate adjustment. A 0.95 on a strong property with a strong borrower is a judgment call rather than a machine decision.

DSCR rental loans: 30-year fixed from 6.80% for the highest credit tier with DSCR 1.20+, before buy down, up to 80% LTV on purchase and 75% on cash-out, loans from $100K, title in your LLC, 42 states.

queue.li_title: How to Choose a DSCR Lender: 12 Questions That Expose the Pretenders | SLA Capital
queue.li_desc: Seasoning, rate honesty, prepay structure, LLC vesting, STR treatment — the questions to ask any lender, with the answers a good one gives.
queue.li:
Every DSCR lender advertises the same three things: low rates, fast closings, no tax returns. The differences that actually cost or make you money live in the details nobody advertises.

Here are the questions that separate the real ones, and we would encourage you to ask them of us as well.

Is your rate sheet published? If hearing a rate requires a phone call and a pitch, the rate can move once you are emotionally committed to the deal. Ours is posted and current.

Is the quoted rate honored at closing? The oldest trick in non-QM is the closing-table bump of 25 to 50 basis points, sprung after you have paid for an appraisal and cannot easily walk. Get the answer in writing. Ours is that the rate you are quoted is the rate you close at.

What are total points and fees, all of them? A 5.99% teaser with three points and three thousand dollars of junk fees loses to a 6.25% with one point. Demand an itemized term sheet before any fee is charged. We charge no application fee and no appraisal fee.

How long is cash-out seasoning? This is the single most consequential number for a BRRRR investor. The DSCR standard is six months, conventional is twelve, and six is what we commit to in writing. If a lender quotes shorter than the standard, get it in writing and read the fine print.

Do I need a lease to close? Good lenders qualify a vacant property on the appraiser's market-rent report. A lender who demands a signed lease is forcing you to rent before you refinance.

What happens when my file hits a wrinkle? Every file has one, whether a title surprise, an appraisal coming in light, or a credit blip. The difference between lenders is whether a human looks for a path or a system spits out a decline. Ask for an example of an exception they have actually made.

The pattern across all twelve questions is simple. Transparency up front predicts execution at the closing table. Lenders who publish rates, itemize fees, and answer seasoning questions with a number tend to run their underwriting the same way.

queue.li_title: BRRRR Method Financing: The Two-Loan Playbook With Real Numbers | SLA Capital
queue.li_desc: The bridge loan that buys and rehabs, the DSCR refinance that pulls your cash back out, a full worked example, and the three rules that set your cycle speed.
queue.li:
Every real estate podcast explains the BRRRR acronym. Almost none of them explain the financing, and the financing is what decides whether you repeat in six months or twelve.

BRRRR is a two-loan strategy. Loan one is a short-term bridge loan that buys and rehabs a property a bank will not touch. It is interest-only, sized off after-repair value, and funds the rehab budget through draws as the work completes. Its job is speed and leverage, and its cost is a project expense rather than a mortgage you live with.

Loan two is a 30-year DSCR refinance, qualified on the property's rent instead of your income, that pays off the bridge loan and returns your capital.

Here is a realistic example. A tired three-bedroom is bought for $180,000 with a $50,000 rehab. A first-time flipper at 85% loan-to-cost gets $195,500 funded and brings roughly $43,500 including closing and carry. The finished property appraises at $300,000 on closed comps. At month six, a 75% cash-out refinance produces a $225,000 loan. After paying off the bridge loan and the refinance costs, about $24,000 comes back. That is more than half the cash returned, $75,000 of equity, and a finished rental, provided market rent covers the new payment.

Three rules set how fast that cycle runs. Seasoning: conventional lenders make you wait 12 months to use the new value, while the DSCR standard, and our written policy, is 6. The DSCR floor: the refinance has to pencil at 1.0 or better on market rent, and strong BRRRR deals leave a cushion. Cash-out LTV: 75% of value is the ceiling, so buying right is what gets all of your money back.

Running both loans through one lender means the second underwrite starts warm. Your entity documents, credit, draw records, and ARV work carry straight over.

At SLA, Fix and Flip bridge loans start from 9.5% with up to 92.5% loan-to-cost for experienced borrowers and closings in as little as 72 hours. DSCR refinances start from 6.80% on a 30-year fixed for the highest credit tier with DSCR 1.20+, before buy down, with no lease required at closing. Loans from $100K in 42 states.

queue.theme: Construction draws / interest on drawn balance
queue.li_title: How Construction Loan Draws Work: Schedules, Inspections & Getting Paid Fast | SLA Capital
queue.li_desc: The request, inspection, and funding cycle, what stalls draws, and the drawn-balance interest term to check on any construction loan.
queue.li:
On a construction loan you do not get the budget at closing. You get it in draws, and the draw process is where good projects keep their momentum and bad lender relationships fall apart.

Lenders fund in stages because the construction budget is lent against work that does not exist yet. Releasing money only against completed, verified work keeps the loan balance tracking the value on the ground. That protects the lender from a half-built project, and it protects you from paying a contractor for framing that has not started.

The cycle is simple. Request: you or your general contractor submit the completed line items with invoices and photos. Inspect: the lender verifies percent complete. App-based inspections with timestamped photos turn around in a day or two, rather than the week or more a traditional site visit can take to schedule. Fund: once the work is confirmed, the wire goes out, on a well-run file within a few business days. A ground-up build typically runs four to seven draws.

Four things slow it down. Draw requests that do not reconcile to the budget, so flag any reallocation between line items before you submit. Missing lien waivers, so collect them as you pay your subs. Work ahead of permits, so keep the paper on site. And radio silence, because a photo update between draws costs nothing and speeds up the next release.

The term worth checking before you sign is how interest accrues. On a drawn-balance loan, a $1,000,000 commitment with $200,000 drawn accrues interest on $200,000. At an illustrative 10% rate, that is roughly $1,667 a month instead of $8,333, and over an 18-month build the difference is real money. Get it in the term sheet.

SLA Capital New Construction loans fund up to 85% of the land purchase and 85% of construction cost, with rates from 10%, 18 or 24 month terms, interest charged only on drawn funds, and draws run through an online portal with app-based inspections. Loans from $100K to $7.5M in 42 states.

queue.li_title: ARV in Fix & Flip Lending: What Lenders Actually Count | SLA Capital
queue.li_desc: How After-Repair Value gets underwritten: comps versus appraisal, LTC versus LTV, and the ARV pitfalls that kill deals at approval.
queue.li:
Every Fix and Flip loan is priced off two numbers: what the property will be worth after the work, and what it costs you to get there. The first number is ARV, and it is where more flips get resized than anywhere else.

ARV is not a Zestimate and it is not the number your wholesaler pitched. It is what a licensed appraiser will sign off on, based on comparable sold properties in the same neighborhood, the same recent window, and the same condition tier, measured against your scope of work.

Investors usually run their own comps at the offer stage. The appraiser runs them differently. Closed sales carry far more weight than active listings. Comps are adjusted for condition, so an as-is cash sale is not a stabilized comp. Your target needs to be bracketed by at least one comp above it and one below. And a scope that is underbuilt for the neighborhood, say laminate where the comps have quartz, pulls the number down.

The mistake we see most often is an offer built on the neighborhood's average price per square foot with no adjustment for finish level. The appraisal comes back 8 to 12 percent low, the loan resizes, and the borrower either covers the gap in cash or walks.

That resize happens because a flip loan faces two leverage tests, and you get the lesser of the two. Loan-to-cost measures the loan against purchase plus rehab and decides your cash to close. Loan-to-ARV caps the loan at a share of the finished value, typically 65 to 75 percent, and protects against thin deals. Miss ARV by 10 percent and the second test binds, even when your cost math worked.

Two habits protect you. Line-item the rehab budget, because a single "kitchen, $28,000" line will not fund a draw, while cabinets, counters, appliances, plumbing, electrical, and flooring broken out will. And overscope rather than underscope, because unused rehab dollars come off at payoff while a forgotten line has to be added mid-project.

SLA Capital Fix and Flip loans start from 9.5% with up to 92.5% loan-to-cost for experienced flippers, 100% of the rehab budget funded through draws, and closings in as little as 72 hours. We review your scope line by line and flag gaps before the appraiser sees the file. Loans from $100K to $3M in 42 states.
